name: Safe Withdrawal Amount (4 % Rule)
description: Gives the first-year withdrawal under a fixed-percentage rule; later withdrawals are raised with inflation.
notes: From Bengen (1994) and the Trinity study: 4 % of a balanced portfolio lasted 30 years in almost all US historical periods.

name: Portfolio Needed for a Withdrawal Rate
description: Gives the savings needed to fund a yearly spending amount at a chosen withdrawal rate ("25 times expenses" at 4 %).
notes: Subtract pensions and other income from spending first.

name: Years a Portfolio Lasts with Fixed Withdrawals
description: Gives how many years fixed withdrawals can be taken before the money runs out.
notes: If w ≤ r × portfolio the money never runs out. Use a real return and real withdrawals to allow for inflation.

name: Retirement Fund Needed for Inflation-Linked Spending
description: Gives the lump sum needed at retirement to pay spending that starts at w and rises with inflation every year for n years (a growing annuity-due).
notes: About 813,000 here for 40,000 a year over 30 years.

name: Annual Saving Needed for a Retirement Goal
description: Gives the yearly (end-of-year) saving needed to reach a target, taking credit for what has already been saved.
notes: Here about 10,130 a year.

name: Years to Financial Independence from a Savings Rate
description: Gives how long it takes, starting from nothing, until savings cover spending at the chosen withdrawal rate. Only the savings rate matters, not the income.
notes: Saving 50 % of income takes about 16.6 years at 5 % real; 10 % takes about 51 years.

name: Defined-Benefit Pension (Final Salary)
description: Gives the yearly pension of a final-salary scheme: accrual rate × years of service × pensionable salary.
notes: A 1/60th scheme after 30 years pays half of final salary.

name: Career-Average Revalued Earnings (CARE) Pension
expression: acc * sum(k, 1, len(earn), at(earn, k) * (1 + rv)^(len(earn) - k))
description: Adds a pension slice for every year of service, each revalued (usually with prices or wages) up to retirement.
notes: Used by many public-sector schemes after moving away from final salary.

name: Pension Replacement Ratio
description: Gives retirement income as a share of earnings just before retirement.
notes: Advisers often suggest aiming for 70–80 % of pre-retirement income.

name: Early Retirement Reduction
description: Applies an actuarial reduction for taking a pension before the normal retirement age.
notes: Reductions of 4–6 % per year are common.

name: Deferred Pension Increase
description: Applies a yearly increase for starting a pension later than the normal age.
notes: Break-even age against claiming early is often in the early 80s.

name: Break-even Age for Delaying a Pension
description: Gives the age at which total payments from delaying catch up with claiming early, ignoring interest.
notes: Delay pays off if you expect to live beyond this age.

name: Pension Funding Ratio
description: Divides a pension plan's assets by the present value of its promised benefits.
notes: Below 100 % the plan is in deficit and sponsors must usually add contributions.

name: Pension Liability Change for a Discount-Rate Move
description: Estimates how much a pension liability changes when the discount rate moves, from its duration and convexity.
notes: Long-duration pension liabilities rise sharply when interest rates fall.

name: Employer Matching Contribution
description: Gives the employer match for a plan that matches a percentage of contributions up to a cap.
notes: Contributing at least up to the cap captures the full match, an immediate return of the match rate.

name: Tax-Deferred Account Value after Tax
description: Grows a contribution tax-free and taxes the whole amount on withdrawal (traditional pension or IRA style).
notes: With the same tax rate now and later this equals a tax-free account funded with after-tax money.

name: Taxable Account Value (Returns Taxed Yearly)
description: Grows an investment whose returns are taxed every year, as in an ordinary taxable account (interest-type income).
notes: Compare with the tax-deferred value to see the benefit of deferral.

name: Age-Based Equity Allocation Rule
description: A rule of thumb for the share of stocks in a portfolio: a constant minus your age.
notes: Target-date funds follow similar glide paths that reduce equity with age.

name: Capital Needed to Fill a Retirement Income Gap
description: Computes the savings needed to cover the part of yearly spending that a pension does not, at a chosen withdrawal rate.
notes: The withdrawal rate is a fraction (0.04 = 4 %). The pension is assumed to rise with prices like the spending.

name: Inflation-Protected Perpetual Withdrawal
description: Computes the first-year withdrawal that can rise with inflation for ever without reducing the real value of the portfolio.
notes: Uses the exact real return (Fisher equation). Returns are assumed steady; real markets vary.

name: Pension with a Linear Deferral Credit
description: Computes a pension that is raised by a fixed percentage for each month it is claimed after the normal age.
notes: The rate per month is set by each pension scheme and can change; enter the current rate. Some schemes compound instead.

name: Years a Portfolio Lasts with Inflation-Rising Withdrawals
description: Computes how many years a portfolio lasts when the withdrawals, taken at the end of each year, rise by a fixed rate.
notes: From the present value of a growing annuity. If port × (r − g) ÷ w is 1 or more, the money never runs out.

name: Total Pension Contributions with Salary Growth
description: Computes the total contributions paid over a career when a fixed share of a salary that grows each year is saved.
notes: Investment returns are not included; this is only the amount paid in.

name: Future Value of Growing Contributions
description: Computes the savings after n years when contributions rise by a fixed rate each year and are paid at the end of each year.
notes: The return and the growth rate must differ; when they are equal the value is n × c × (1 + r)^(n − 1).

name: Present Value of Future Earnings (Human Capital)
description: Computes the value today of the earnings still to come in a working life, a measure of human capital used in retirement planning.
notes: Earnings are taken at the end of each year and grow at a steady rate. The discount rate should reflect how secure the job is.

name: Real Value of a Partly Indexed Pension
description: Computes the purchasing power, in today's money, of a pension that is raised each year by only part of inflation.
notes: A share of 1 means full indexation (the real value stays the same); 0 means a fixed pension.
